change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name leaks the website host that is hidden for restricted users
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. That is a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-59). `website_name` is not in that list. The only guard is `include_website_name` (line 153), and it is never called: this serializer's conditional hooks use the `include_x?` form (lines 9, 18, 28, 117 and others), and `include_website_name` has no `?`. So `website_name` is always serialized, and the host of a hidden website is sent to anonymous users in the user JSON, including the preloaded JSON in users_controller.rb:51. The template then shows the globe icon and the host name for a user whose website the code means to hide. Before this change the name was derived client-side from `model.website`, which was absent in this case. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or make it return `include_website? && website.present?`. Add a spec for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous scope.

findings.title: Displayed website name goes stale after the user edits their website
findings.body: `websiteName` was a computed property on `model.website`, so it updated as soon as the website changed. It is now the server-computed `model.website_name`. `User.save` (models/user.js.es6:166-217) sends `website` but only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response, and the preferences `save` action (controllers/preferences.js.es6:117-123) only updates `name` and `bio_cooked`. The profile page therefore shows the old host, or an old name when the website was cleared, until the user object is reloaded. This assumes the preferences route shares the parent user route's model, which I did not check. Also set `website_name` from the PUT response, or recompute it after save.

findings.title: website_name logic is fragile and drops information
findings.body:
Several problems in `website_name`:
- `URI(...)` is called three times, and `rescue nil` is a statement modifier that hides every error.
- A website with no scheme, such as `example.com`, parses with a nil host. No name is shown, and the user's link is still set. The old client code behaved the same way here, but now there is no fallback.
- `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` compares label counts. It treats unrelated hosts such as `a.example.com` and `b.other.org` as non-siblings. Siblings with a longer public suffix, such as `x.example.co.uk` and `y.example.co.uk`, also compare equal, but the check only works for these sibling cases.
- `"." << website_host` mutates a literal string; use `".#{website_host}"`.
- A path of `/` produces a trailing-slash name such as `example.com/`.
Parse once into a local variable and extract the comparison into a small helper.

findings.title: Missing coverage for sibling-subdomain branch, invalid or blank website, and restricted viewers
findings.body: The three examples cover only the same-host branch, the parent-domain branch, and the unrelated-domain branch. They do not cover the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (line 146 of the serializer). They do not cover a blank or invalid website, where `website_name` should be omitted. They do not cover a TL0 user seen by an anonymous scope. That last case would have caught the missing `include_website_name?` hook.

contracts.action: Profile header shows website host from server-computed website_name instead of client-computed websiteName
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed controller computed property websiteName (controllers/user.js.es6, base lines 17-21) derived from model.website; gated by the untrusted_attributes visibility rules for website.
contracts.before_after: Before: the name was derived client-side from model.website, so it was absent whenever website was omitted for restricted viewers and updated live on edit. After: the name comes from the serializer. It is always sent because include_website_name lacks the `?`, and it is not refreshed after save.
contracts.visible_effect: Anonymous viewers of a TL0 profile see the globe icon and host even though website is hidden. After editing the website in preferences, the profile shows the old name until reload.
contracts.failure_mode: No error is raised, so the wrong value is silent. An invalid URL gives a nil host and the name is omitted silently.

summary: The PR moves the website display name to the server and adds a rule that shows the full path when the website is on the same domain as the instance. I found two things to fix. First, `include_website_name` lacks the `?`, so it is never called and `website_name` bypasses the TL0-anonymous restriction that hides `website`. That leaks the host of a hidden website. Second, the client no longer recomputes the name after the user edits their website, so the profile shows the old name until reload. I also left two lower-severity notes: the host-matching code is fragile, and the specs miss the sibling-subdomain, blank-website and restricted-viewer cases.
